title: OSHA general industry bloodborne pathogens practice questions
description: Free OSHA bloodborne pathogens practice questions on 29 CFR 1910.1030. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: What does the 1910.1030(b) definition of handwashing facilities say such a facility provides?

options.A: A sink with hot water and a shared cloth towel
options.B: An adequate supply of running potable water, soap, and single-use towels or air-drying machines
options.C: A supply of antiseptic towelettes only
options.D: A bottle of alcohol hand rub at each workstation

questions.explanation: "Handwashing facilities means a facility providing an adequate supply of running potable water, soap, and single-use towels or air-drying machines."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the standard's definition of personal protective equipment, how are general work clothes such as uniforms that are not intended to protect against a hazard treated?

options.A: As PPE whenever the employer issues them
options.B: As PPE when worn in patient care areas
options.C: As PPE only if the employer launders them
options.D: As not being personal protective equipment

questions.explanation: General work clothes (e.g., uniforms, pants, shirts or blouses) "not intended to function as protection against a hazard are not considered to be personal protective equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employer required to have an Exposure Control Plan is identifying, evaluating and selecting engineering and work practice controls. From whom must it solicit input under 1910.1030(c)(1)(v)?

options.A: Non-managerial employees responsible for direct patient care who are potentially exposed to injuries from contaminated sharps
options.B: Only the facility's managers
options.C: The sales representatives of sharps device makers
options.D: The local health department

questions.explanation: The employer "shall solicit input from non-managerial employees responsible for direct patient care who are potentially exposed to injuries from contaminated sharps" and "shall document the solicitation in the Exposure Control Plan."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How must the exposure determination treat the use of personal protective equipment?

options.A: It counts only exposure that remains after PPE is worn
options.B: It assumes every employee wears gloves at all times
options.C: It is made without regard to the use of PPE
options.D: It covers only employees who refuse to wear PPE

questions.explanation: The rule states: "This exposure determination shall be made without regard to the use of personal protective equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Universal precautions and work practice controls
questions.question: A blood specimen could puncture its primary container. What does 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiii)(C) require?

options.A: Placing the primary container within a secondary container that is puncture-resistant in addition to the other required characteristics
options.B: Wrapping the primary container in adhesive tape
options.C: Removing the label so the container is not mistaken for waste
options.D: Hand-carrying the primary container with no outer container

questions.explanation: "If the specimen could puncture the primary container, the primary container shall be placed within a secondary container which is puncture-resistant in addition to the above characteristics."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Universal precautions and work practice controls
questions.question: Equipment that cannot be fully decontaminated is being sent out for servicing. What must the readily observable label attached under 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiv)(A) state?

options.A: The name of the employee who last used it
options.B: The date the equipment was bought
options.C: The diagnosis of the patient it was used on
options.D: Which portions remain contaminated

questions.explanation: A readily observable label "shall be attached to the equipment stating which portions remain contaminated."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Universal precautions and work practice controls
questions.question: At a field site where handwashing facilities are not feasible, an employee cleans up with antiseptic towelettes. What must follow under 1910.1030(d)(2)(iv)?

options.A: Nothing more; towelettes fully replace handwashing
options.B: Washing hands with soap and running water as soon as feasible
options.C: Wearing a second pair of gloves for the rest of the shift
options.D: Reporting the use of towelettes to OSHA

questions.explanation: "When antiseptic hand cleansers or towelettes are used, hands shall be washed with soap and running water as soon as feasible."

questions.question: When is personal protective equipment considered "appropriate" under 1910.1030?

options.A: When it is the lowest-cost model available
options.B: When the employee picks it out personally
options.C: Only if it does not let blood or other potentially infectious materials pass through to or reach the employee's clothes, skin, eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes under normal conditions of use, for as long as it will be used
options.D: When it is worn for no more than one hour

questions.explanation: PPE is appropriate "only if it does not permit blood or other potentially infectious materials to pass through to or reach" the employee's work clothes, street clothes, undergarments, skin, eyes, mouth, or other mucous membranes "under normal conditions of use and for the duration of time which the protective equipment will be used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.1030(d)(3)(ix)(C), when may utility gloves be decontaminated for re-use?

options.A: Only if they were worn for less than one hour
options.B: Never; they must be thrown away after each use
options.C: If the integrity of the glove is not compromised
options.D: Only once they show cracks, so the cracks can be cleaned

questions.explanation: "Utility gloves may be decontaminated for re-use if the integrity of the glove is not compromised." They must be discarded if they are cracked, peeling, torn, punctured or otherwise deteriorated.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When does 1910.1030(d)(3)(xii) require surgical caps or hoods and/or shoe covers or boots to be worn?

options.A: In instances when gross contamination can reasonably be anticipated, such as autopsies or orthopaedic surgery
options.B: Only in HIV and HBV research laboratories
options.C: Whenever gloves are worn
options.D: Only when the employee asks for them

questions.explanation: "Surgical caps or hoods and/or shoe covers or boots shall be worn in instances when gross contamination can reasonably be anticipated (e.g., autopsies, orthopaedic surgery)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Plastic wrap covers a piece of equipment as a protective covering. Under 1910.1030(d)(4)(ii)(B), when must it be removed and replaced?

options.A: Once a week, on a fixed day
options.B: Only after a spill has been reported to OSHA
options.C: Only when it is torn
options.D: As soon as feasible when it becomes overtly contaminated, or at the end of the workshift if it may have become contaminated during the shift

questions.explanation: Protective coverings such as plastic wrap "shall be removed and replaced as soon as feasible when they become overtly contaminated or at the end of the workshift if they may have become contaminated during the shift."

questions.question: During use, how must containers for contaminated sharps be kept?

options.A: Laid on their side so sharps slide in easily
options.B: Maintained upright throughout use, replaced routinely and not allowed to overfill
options.C: Emptied by hand when full and put back in service
options.D: Stored in a locked room away from where sharps are used

questions.explanation: During use, sharps containers shall be easily accessible, "Maintained upright throughout use" and "Replaced routinely and not be allowed to overfill."

questions.topic: Hepatitis B vaccination and post-exposure follow-up
questions.question: An employer wants employees to complete a prescreening program before they can receive hepatitis B vaccination. What does 1910.1030(f)(2)(ii) say?

options.A: Prescreening is required for every employee before vaccination
options.B: The employer shall not make participation in a prescreening program a prerequisite for receiving the vaccination
options.C: Prescreening may be required only for employees over age 40
options.D: Prescreening may be required if the employee pays for it

questions.explanation: The rule states: "The employer shall not make participation in a prescreening program a prerequisite for receiving hepatitis B vaccination."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Hepatitis B vaccination and post-exposure follow-up
questions.question: The U.S. Public Health Service recommends a routine hepatitis B booster dose at a future date. What does 1910.1030(f)(2)(v) require of the employer?

options.A: Make the booster dose(s) available in accordance with (f)(1)(ii), including at no cost to the employee
options.B: Nothing; booster doses are outside the standard
options.C: Offer the booster only to employees who ask, at their own cost
options.D: Offer the booster only at the next annual training

questions.explanation: If a routine booster dose is recommended by the U.S. Public Health Service, "such booster dose(s) shall be made available in accordance with section (f)(1)(ii)." That section requires it to be "Made available at no cost to the employee".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Hepatitis B vaccination and post-exposure follow-up
questions.question: The healthcare professional's written opinion for post-exposure evaluation is limited to certain information. What does 1910.1030(f)(5) say about all other findings or diagnoses?

options.A: They are sent to the employee's supervisor
options.B: They are posted with the sharps injury log
options.C: They are added to the employee's training record
options.D: They shall remain confidential and shall not be included in the written report

questions.explanation: "All other findings or diagnoses shall remain confidential and shall not be included in the written report."

questions.question: How must the required warning labels be affixed under 1910.1030(g)(1)(i)(D)?

options.A: Loosely taped so they can be moved to other containers
options.B: On a clipboard hung near the container
options.C: As close as feasible to the container by string, wire, adhesive, or other method that prevents their loss or unintentional removal
options.D: Only on the door of the room holding the container

questions.explanation: "Labels shall be affixed as close as feasible to the container by string, wire, adhesive, or other method that prevents their loss or unintentional removal."

questions.question: What does 1910.1030(g)(2)(vi) require of the material used in bloodborne pathogens training?

options.A: That it be appropriate in content and vocabulary to the educational level, literacy, and language of employees
options.B: That it be in English only
options.C: That it be a video with no live trainer
options.D: That it be written at a college reading level

questions.explanation: "Material appropriate in content and vocabulary to educational level, literacy, and language of employees shall be used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A new procedure changes an employee's occupational exposure. What does 1910.1030(g)(2)(v) say about the additional training the employer must provide?

options.A: It must repeat the entire training program
options.B: It may wait until the next annual session
options.C: It is not required if the employee was trained within the year
options.D: It may be limited to addressing the new exposures created

questions.explanation: Employers "shall provide additional training when changes such as modification of tasks or procedures or institution of new tasks or procedures affect the employee's occupational exposure. The additional training may be limited to addressing the new exposures created."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Without the employee's express written consent, to whom may the medical records required by 1910.1030(h)(1) be disclosed or reported?

options.A: To the employee's direct supervisor
options.B: To any coworker who asks
options.C: To no person within or outside the workplace, except as required by the section or as may be required by law
options.D: To the employer's insurance broker

questions.explanation: The records must be "Kept confidential" and "Not disclosed or reported without the employee's express written consent to any person within or outside the workplace except as required by this section or as may be required by law."

questions.question: Which item must the sharps injury log contain, at a minimum, under 1910.1030(h)(5)(i)?

options.A: The injured employee's home address
options.B: The type and brand of device involved in the incident
options.C: The purchase price of the device
options.D: The name of the device's sales representative

questions.explanation: The log shall contain, at a minimum, "The type and brand of device involved in the incident", the department or work area where the exposure incident occurred, and an explanation of how it occurred.
